speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present and on what scale would you rate the intensity of the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture).

The history of forceful retching following alcohol consumption, followed by sudden onset of chest pain and choking, is highly specific for esophageal rupture. I will now request a CT scan of the chest with contrast to confirm the diagnosis and check for mediastinal emphysema or pleural effusion.
